title: Could be so much better
text:
I genuinely love this app and use it most days, but it could be so much better with a few small tweaks! I get that not everyone would want these changes, but I think the workaround would be to make them optional so at least some people can choose them if they want:

1) When I trialled the paid version, I was really hoping that the rooms (the ones that you decorate using the coins you’ve earned by cleaning) would be individual to each household member. I obviously want the tasks to be shared but, for me, I like to furnish them in a way that’s fun/exciting for me, not for the whole household. The idea that others could come in and play about with the rooms I’ve curated over time by cleaning just gets rid of the novelty of it for me. 

2) Also on the paid version, there’s no option to have fully private rooms for different household members. This isn’t a huge thing but it’d be nice to have the option for my bedroom, for example, to be private just for me. I trust my housemate but also would feel self conscious and demotivated if they could see how well I was keeping on top of cleaning my bedroom.

3) For some reason you can sort the room’s by cleanliness but there’s no option to just sort all tasks by cleanliness/when you last completed them. I’d find this so useful as sometimes focusing on the room as a whole isn’t the best option for me. I get that the AI feature in the paid version sort of does this a bit, but not really in a straightforward way. I just want to be able to sort *all* household tasks from dirtiest to cleanest!

title: Useful but restrictive for no reason
text:
I really like this as a way to keep organised but two things have been bugging me. 

The coins given for completing tasks are really low compared to the high cost of the decor items, making the gamification aspect a bit underwhelming. I can clean my whole place and only end up with about 20 gold, when some items are at at 70 gold. That means I can’t buy an item per day and since the shop resets daily, I just miss out on that item. The shop also takes too long to reset and there could be an option to reset it early if you didn’t want to purchase the existing items, like how it works in Finch. I’d really love the decor game aspect to work a bit better to make cleaning a little more fun.

I’d also like to be able to just see all of my tasks in one big list, but the only way to really view is by going into each room and it’s a bit tedious at times.

title: Good but quite negative
text:
This is probably the best app out there for tracking chores atm (that I could find) but I do find it quite negative. 

I really like tracking my activity as I often struggle to do this independently and can often feel overwhelmed by the chores. This helps streamline the approach and makes sure that I am doing what is most needed. It feels like a positive achievement and is genuinely really helping. 

However: 

When you have just done a chore it says, ‘shiny clean’ but very quickly goes into the orange ‘good enough’. 

The red section can appear many days before you are actually due to clean, making you feel like you are failing, even though the chore doesn’t need to be done yet. I have actually started extending times to reflect this. 

Ideally, I would like a green bar that gradually gets lighter on one side. On the bright green could be ‘shiny clean’ on the other side could be ‘ready to clean’ so you can choose when to clean along the shaded line but without the negative guilt language or the negative association of the red colour (which is used for when you have got something wrong). 

If it was keeping the colours, I would say the red should only show red on the day it needs doing, not before (one of mine is red about a week before it is due- I’ve noticed I then go on a mad clean to try and get rid of the red, only to realise it could have waited a bit and I didn’t need to get so stressed). Maybe also change the yellow to be clean (shiny clean -> clean -> ready to clean). 

I know it might not sound like a lot, but it really does make a difference. 

I like this concept but I will be keeping my eye out for one with more a more encouraging and positive feel. Shame as I think it’s great to use.

title: Reminders that do t remind you in time
text:
If you says smth needs cleaning once a week. It’ll remind you after 10 days or so. So if the reminders to clean don’t let you know smth needs doing in time you want it to, what’s the point???
And on the main page you see all the rooms and have to manually go and check each of them to see which tasks are overdue where. 
It’s supposed to make my cleaning life easier but so far it reliably served me only as notepad. 
I had free trial and schedule seams like a great idea. But as it reminds you to do stuff whenever it wishes instead of when I want it I’m not paying for subscription. 
Also for only one person subscription should be cheaper as I can’t use so many features that are useful for groups.

title: My Honest Opinion
text: It’s ok if you only want to add you but all of the fun features they show you have to pay for, like you can’t add family members without the premium version or create a daily schedule, but so far from my use of it, it seems like a fun way of organising all of the chores you have to do to make it more interactive and motivational. If you don’t mind not adding anyone else without paying, it’s a great alternative to just writing a list down.

title: Works fine, ludicrous subscription cost
text: The app works like it’s supposed to to be fair.    If you’re cleaning whilst listening to music it will stop whatever media is playing every time you clear a job though.  And the subscription cost is frankly predatory, I do not see how it can possibly be justified by the bare-bones nature of the app with the bugs that it has.  I would happily have paid a fiver for a one-off purchase for this, but continuous payment of, I think, £50 a year is outrageous.

title: Needs better notifications
text: Good, but needs better notifications. Getting a notification in the morning when there's nothing to clean is a a bit useless, and I end up ignoring them. Would appreciate it if the notifications were personalised to the task, e.g. a notification when a task moves to 'Get down to work' and another if it's 'What's that smell?'.

title: Functional to a point
text:
After you mark one time tasks as complete they reappear at full degradation and nuke your room score. As long as you don’t use them the app is quite functional.
Would love to see a task chaining option whereby upon completing a task it triggers a countdown for a new pre coded task so you can break down steps to completion for “one task” allowing you to automate executive functioning.

title: Sort of useful but could be so much better
text:
The app itself is useful. My partner uses it heavily. However as someone with ADHD, I frequently forget to mark tasks I’ve done, or forget to look at what needs doing. 
It would be great if you could create QR codes or use NFC stickers to have an easy way to scan/tap to mark a task as completed.

title: OK could be better
text:
It’s great that you can organise and recognise tasks however the premium features are not helpful to me as I can’t set my own schedule for tasks in particular the random nature of assigned tasks splits the dusting and vacuuming of rooms. 

There are a few issues / changes I feel would be an improvement:
- to be able to quantify how needed a task is in proportional increments.
- to be able to rank tasks (every week / important occasional tasks or specific tasks for a certain day)
- identify more than three important tasks (or minimum to do each week)
- organise my own schedule or assign tasks to a person

title: Why does everything need a subscription?
text: I spent 5 minutes setting up tasks for the bedroom depending on difficulty, and frequency, only to find out at the end I need a subscription to be able to share it with other members of my household. It’s ridiculous! Why does every app require a subscription these days? Immediately deleted. I’d rather get a whiteboard and write our tasks on it.
